questions.q: Ashokan inscriptions suggest that the 'Pradeshika', 'Rajuka' and 'Yukta' were important officers at the
questions.e: Ashokan inscriptions suggest that 'Pradeshika', 'Rajuka' and 'Yukta' were important officers at the district-level administration. Pradeshika was the overall in-charge of the district. District administration was under the charge of Rajukas, who had functions similar to modern collectors and held authority to reward or punish. The Yukta was a junior officer providing secretarial and accounting assistance. These officials performed duties like land survey, revenue collection, and maintaining law and order. The Third Edict mentions their need to go on inspection tours every five years while preaching Dhamma.

questions.q: With reference to the Mahajanapadas in ancient India, consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Matsya - Viratnagara 2️⃣ Shurasena - Mathura 3️⃣ Kosala - Indraprastha 4️⃣ Anga - Champa. How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Matsya (Rajasthan) had its capital at Viratnagara. Shurasena's capital was Mathura. Anga's capital was Champa. These three pairs are correct. Kosala's capital was Shravasti; Indraprastha was the capital of the Kuru Mahajanapada. Mahajanapadas were territorial states rising between 600 BCE to 400 BCE with fortified capitals acting as administrative and trade hubs.

questions.q: The text 'Therigatha' is a part of which of the following Buddhist compositions?
questions.e: The Therigatha is a unique Buddhist text consisting of verses composed by bhikkhunis (nuns). It is part of the Sutta Pitaka, specifically within the Khuddaka Nikaya. The Sutta Pitaka contains Buddha's essential teachings divided into five nikayas. In contrast, the Vinaya Pitaka contains rules for the monastic order , and the Abhidhamma Pitaka deals with philosophical matters. Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa are Pali chronicles from Sri Lanka containing regional history.

questions.q: The Ganeshwar-Jodhpura cultural complex was most closely associated with which of the following cultures?
questions.e: The Ganeshwar-Jodhpura cultural complex was a Chalcolithic culture located in North-Eastern Rajasthan. It was situated near Khetri copper deposits and is believed to have been the largest copper-producing community in South Asia around 3000 BCE. This culture likely supplied copper to the Harappans. Excavations date Jodhpura to 2900-2500 BCE and Ganeshwar to 2500-2000 BCE.

questions.q: With reference to ancient India (600-322 BC), consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Asmaka - Godavari 2️⃣ Kamboja - Vipas 3️⃣ Avanti - Mahanadi 4️⃣ Kosala - Sarayu. How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Asmaka was located in the Godavari valley. Kosala was situated along the Sarayu river, which divided it into northern and southern parts. These two pairs are correct. Kamboja is associated with the Jhelum (Vitasta) river, not the Vipas (Beas). Avanti was in the Malwa region; the Mahanadi does not flow through it.

questions.q: The philosophical debate between Gargi, a woman scholar and Yajnavalkya, a sage is mentioned in detail in which among the following Upanishads?
questions.e: The debate between the rishika Gargi and the sage Yajnavalkya regarding the nature of reality and Brahman is recorded in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad. The Katha Upanishad focuses on Nachiketa and Yama discussing death. The Chhandogya Upanishad features the teaching of "Tat Tvam Asi" by Aruni to Shvetaketu. The Mundaka Upanishad distinguishes between higher and lower knowledge and is the source of "Satyameva Jayate".

questions.q: With reference to Jain philosophy, which of the following best describes the principle of "Anekantavada"?
o: It is an idea which suggests that everything in the universe whether living or non-living being has a soul of its own.
It is an idea which suggests that the truth has many aspects and cannot be fully described by any single statement.
It means detachment from material possessions and limiting oneself to what is truly necessary in life.
It is a practice that involves voluntarily fasting unto death.
questions.e: Anekantavada translates to "not just one" aspect. It posits that reality/truth is complex with many facets, and no single statement can fully capture it. It encourages intellectual humility and tolerance by suggesting different viewpoints can be partially true. Other Jain doctrines include Ahimsa (non-injury), Satya (truth), Asteya (non-stealing), Aparigraha (non-possession), and Brahmacharya (chastity).

questions.q: With reference to the history of ancient India, consider the following: Both Buddhist and Jain School of Thought: 1️⃣ believed in the concept of karma 2️⃣ rejected the authority of the Vedas 3️⃣ believed in the concept of rebirth 4️⃣ rejected the existence of the soul 5️⃣ emphasised on avoidance of extremities of penance and enjoyment. Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Both traditions accepted Karma as a moral law and believed in Rebirth until liberation. Both rejected Vedic authority and Brahmanical supremacy. However, Buddhism rejected the permanent soul (Anatta), while Jainism firmly believed in the eternal soul (Jiva). Buddhism advocated the "Middle Path," whereas Jainism emphasized extreme penance and asceticism.

questions.q: The quotation: "Not by water is one made pure... But one is pure in whom truth and dharma reside. Conquering oneself is greater than conquering a thousand men on the battlefield..." is attributed to:
questions.e: Gautama Buddha emphasized inner moral purity and righteous conduct (Dhamma) over external rituals like ritual bathing. He taught that self-conquest—overcoming greed, anger, and ignorance—is the highest victory, far superior to military achievements.

questions.q: Arrange the following ancient Indian cities from east to west: 1️⃣ Pragjyotishapura 2️⃣ Śhibipura 3️⃣ Rājagriha 4️⃣ Champa.
questions.e: Pragjyotishapura (Assam) is the easternmost. Champa (Eastern Bihar) lies to its west. Rajagriha (Central Bihar) is further west. Shibipura (North-western plains/Pakistan) is the westernmost.

questions.q: The river mentioned most in early Vedic literature is:
questions.e: The Aryans lived in 'Sapta Sindhu' (Land of Seven Rivers). Among these, the Sindhu (Indus) is the most frequently mentioned river in early Vedic literature. The seven rivers included Sindhu, Vipash, Vitasta, Parushni, Asikni, Shutudri, and Saraswati.

questions.q: Consider the following information: 1️⃣ Contemporary of Gautama Buddha and Mahavira 2️⃣ First Buddhist Council held during his reign 3️⃣ Developed Pataliputra as a political centre. This describes:
questions.e: Ajatasatru (Haryanka dynasty) was a contemporary of Buddha and Mahavira. He patronized the First Buddhist Council at Rajgriha to preserve teachings. He also fortified Pataliputra due to its strategic riverine location.

questions.q: With reference to the ancient Indian scholar Panini: 1️⃣ Contemporary to Mauryan King Ashoka 2️⃣ Known for composing the Astadhyayi 3️⃣ Associated with the ancient centre of learning at Vikramsila. Which is/are correct?
questions.e: Panini lived around the 4th century BCE, preceding Ashoka (3rd century BCE). He composed the Astadhyayi, the foundational scientific treatise on Sanskrit grammar. He was associated with Takshashila University, not Vikramsila (which was founded in the 8th-9th century CE).

questions.q: How many of the following were port cities/towns in ancient India? 1️⃣ Bharukachchha 2️⃣ Sopārā 3️⃣ Pratishthāna 4️⃣ Suvarnagiri.
questions.e: Bharukachchha (Gujarat) and Sopara (Maharashtra) were major ancient ports on the western coast. Pratishthana was an important inland trading centre on the Dakshinapatha. Suvarnagiri was a provincial capital in southern India, not a port.

questions.q: From which one of the following factory sites were limestone and chert blades mass produced and sent to various Harappan settlements in Sindh?
questions.e: The Sukkur and Rohri Hills in Sindh, Pakistan, were major sources of limestone and chert. Harappans mass-produced blades and tools at these factory sites for distribution to other settlements in the region.

questions.q: In context to Buddhism, which statement best refers to the doctrine of 'patichcha-samuppada'?
o: All dharmas exist continuously, in the past, present and the future.
All the things in this world exist independently without any cause.
Everything in this universe has a cause, and nothing exists and happens without a cause.
The world and its objects are not permanent, but exist only momentarily.
questions.e: Pratitya-samutpada is the Buddhist theory of causation (Dependent Origination) . it states that nothing exists independently; everything depends on causes and conditions in a cycle of twelve links. It is a middle path between eternalism and annihilationism.

questions.q: Kautilya identified seven organs of state under Saptanga theory. How many of the following are among them? 1️⃣ Fortified towns (Durga) 2️⃣ Treasury (Kosha) 3️⃣ Territory and population (Janpada) 4️⃣ Coercive Power (Danda).
questions.e: Kautilya’s Saptanga theory includes: Swami (King), Amatya (Ministers), Janpada (Territory/Population), Durga (Fort), Kosha (Treasury), Danda (Army), and Mitra (Ally). Durga represents strategic defense. Kosha sustains the polity. Janpada includes land and people. Danda refers to coercive military/police power.

questions.q: How many of the following sites are known for the Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka? 1️⃣ Sarnath 2️⃣ Dhauli 3️⃣ Mansehra 4️⃣ Kalsi 5️⃣ Kandahar.
questions.e: Dhauli, Mansehra, Kalsi, and Kandahar are sites of Major Rock Edicts. Sarnath is the site of a Pillar Edict/Minor Pillar Edict, not a Major Rock Edict.

questions.q: With reference to Sohgaura copper plate inscription: 1️⃣ Written in Prakrit using Brahmi script 2️⃣ Issued during the reign of Ashoka 3️⃣ Describes poor management of food crisis. Which are incorrect?
questions.e: Statement I is correct: it is in Prakrit and Brahmi. Statement II is incorrect: it was issued under Chandragupta Maurya, not Ashoka. Statement III is incorrect: it describes proactive state measures (granaries) for famine relief, not poor management.

questions.q: The national motto "Satyameva Jayate" is taken from:
questions.e: "Satyameva Jayate" (Truth Alone Triumphs) is from the Mundaka Upanishad. It was adopted as India's national motto and is inscribed below the Lion Capital of Ashoka in the National Emblem.

questions.q: Consider the following: 1️⃣ Isampur was a center of stone tool manufacture in Karnataka situated near Kamta Halla 2️⃣ A Paleolithic blade length is more than twice its width. Which are correct?
questions.e: Isampur (Gulbarga, Karnataka) is a significant archaeological factory site near a water source. In Paleolithic terminology, a blade is a specific flake tool defined by having a length more than twice its width.

questions.q: How many of the following cities were located on Dakshinapatha? 1️⃣ Ujjaiyini 2️⃣ Kaushambi 3️⃣ Bhrigukaccha.
questions.e: The Dakshinapatha was a major southern trade route starting from Kaushambi, passing through Ujjaiyini, and extending to the port of Bhrigukaccha (Broach). It also connected to Pratishthana.

questions.q: Regarding the Shunga Period: 1️⃣ Witnessed revival of Vedic rituals like Ashvamedha 2️⃣ Yoga Sūtras compiled by Patañjali 3️⃣ Construction of Bharhut Stupa was initiated. Which are correct?
questions.e: Rulers like Pushyamitra Shunga performed the Ashvamedha sacrifice, marking a Vedic revival. Patanjali compiled the foundational Yoga Sutras during this era. Statement III is incorrect: Bharhut Stupa was likely built under Ashoka, though the Shungas added the ornate railings and reliefs.

questions.q: Which caves have a yaksha sculpture stating "made by Kanahadasa, a goldsmith"?
questions.e: A Yaksha sculpture found at Pitalkhora Caves (Maharashtra) carries an inscription "kanhadāsena hiramakarena kāța". This indicates that a goldsmith (Kanahadasa) crafted a stone sculpture during the Satavahana period.

questions.q: Regarding Vedic sacrifices: 1️⃣ Shrauta involve three fires (Garhapatya, Ahavaniya, Dakshinagni) 2️⃣ Garhapatya is in a square pit and Ahavaniya in a circular pit. Which are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: shrauta rituals use the Tretagni (three fires). Statement 2 is incorrect: the Garhapatya fire is in a circular pit, while the Ahavaniya is in a square pit.

questions.q: With reference to King Kharavela: 1️⃣ Ruler of Mahameghavahana dynasty 2️⃣ Donated Uadaygiri/Khandgiri to Buddhist monks 3️⃣ Hathigumpha inscription accounts his military campaigns. Which are correct?
questions.e: Kharavela belonged to the Mahameghavahana (Chedi) dynasty of Kalinga. The Hathigumpha inscription is the primary source detailing his reign and military deeds. Statement II is incorrect: Kharavela was a devout Jain; the caves were for Jain monks (Nirgranthas), not Buddhists.

questions.q: Which describes Rta/Rita in Vedic hymns?
o: The path of liberation achieved through renunciation of worldly life.
The system of ritual sacrifices performed to please the gods.
The moral code enforced primarily through royal authority.
questions.e: Rta is the principle of natural and cosmic order in the Vedas. It systematically connects order, rule, and truth, governing the universe and moral systems. Human action relative to these principles is Karma.

questions.q: Regarding Kanishka: 1️⃣ Rule marks beginning of "Saka era" 2️⃣ Supporter of Hinayana Buddhism 3️⃣ Patron of Vasumitra and Nagarjuna. Which are correct?
questions.e: Kanishka's accession (78 CE) is associated with the Saka era used in India's national calendar. He patronized scholars like Vasumitra and Nagarjuna. Statement II is incorrect: Kanishka actively supported Mahayana Buddhism, spreading it to Central Asia and China.

questions.q: How many of the following are Chalcolithic cultures? 1️⃣ Kayatha 2️⃣ Malwa 3️⃣ Jorwe.
questions.e: All three are non-Harappan Chalcolithic cultures where stone and copper were used. Kayatha (MP, c. 2100-2000 BC) , Malwa (MP, c. 1700-1400 BC) , and Jorwe (Maharashtra, c. 1400-700 BC) are key examples.

questions.q: Regarding Megasthenes’ Indica: 1️⃣ Slavery was a punishment for crimes 2️⃣ Society divided into seven occupational classes 3️⃣ Highlighted women in politics 4️⃣ Brahmanas/Shramanas were tax exempt. Which are correct?
questions.e: Megasthenes claimed there was no slavery in India (contradicting Kautilya). He correctly identified seven occupational classes (philosophers, cultivators, etc.). Statements III and IV are incorrect: he made no mention of women in politics and did not explicitly state Shramanas were tax-exempt.

questions.q: Regarding the Indus Valley Civilization: 1️⃣ Predominantly secular with non-dominating religion 2️⃣ Cotton was used for manufacturing textiles. Which are correct?
questions.e: Harappan farmers were the first to weave cotton. The civilization was predominantly secular; while religious elements existed, they did not dominate the social or political scene.

questions.q: Which dynasty was established earliest?
questions.e: The Shunga dynasty was founded in 185 BCE. The Kanvas succeeded them in 73 BCE. The Shakas (1st century BCE) and Kushanas (1st century CE) were established later.

questions.q: How many pairs are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Nageshwar - Gujarat 2️⃣ Manda - J&K 3️⃣ Mitathal - Maharashtra 4️⃣ Daimabad - Haryana.
questions.e: Nageshwar is in Gujarat and Manda is the northernmost site in J&K. Mitathal is located in Haryana , and Daimabad is in Maharashtra.

questions.q: Which crops were cultivated by the Indus Valley Civilization? 1️⃣ Wheat 2️⃣ Barley 3️⃣ Sesame 4️⃣ Maize.
questions.e: Harappans cultivated wheat, barley, sesame, peas, and cotton. Maize was introduced much later by Europeans and was not known to the Harappans.

questions.q: Regarding Stone Age in India: 1️⃣ Identified by tool technology 2️⃣ No regional variations 3️⃣ Evolved uniformly/unilinearly. Which is correct?
questions.e: Periods are identified by stone tool types (e.g., microliths in Mesolithic). Statements 2 and 3 are incorrect: there were significant regional variations and cultures did not evolve in a neat unilinear fashion across the subcontinent.

questions.q: Regarding Harappan architecture: 1️⃣ Rectangular grid pattern with roads at right angles 2️⃣ Uniform average brick size across cities. Which are correct?
questions.e: Cities followed a grid layout where streets intersected at right angles. Bricks were standardized in a ratio of 1:2:4 (height:breadth:length) and used across all settlements.

questions.q: Which Buddhist text lists the sixteen Mahajanapadas?
questions.e: The Anguttara Nikaya (part of Sutta-Pitaka) provides the list of 16 Mahajanapadas. The Jaina Bhagavati Sutra and the Buddhist Mahavastu also list 16, though with some differences.

questions.q: Regarding the Harappan script: 1️⃣ Written left to right 2️⃣ Long inscriptions 3️⃣ Alphabetical. Which are correct?
questions.e: All statements are incorrect. The script was mostly written right to left. Inscriptions are very short (average 5 signs). The script was pictographic (375-400 signs), not alphabetical.

questions.q: In Mauryan administration, the term "Samaharta" refers to:
o: administering justice and presiding over royal courts.
supervising trade, commerce, and urban guilds.
commanding the standing army and supervising military garrisons.
questions.e: The Samaharta was the chief revenue officer responsible for collecting taxes from land, fines, and other state incomes to finance the empire.

questions.q: Regarding ancient coinage: 1️⃣ Earliest Punch-marked coins were silver/copper 2️⃣ Indo-Greeks were first to issue gold 3️⃣ Kushanas first to issue images of monarch 4️⃣ No bilingual inscriptions. Which are correct?
questions.e: Punch-marked coins (6th century BCE) were silver/copper. Indo-Greeks were the first to issue gold coins in India. Statement III is incorrect: Indo-Greeks, not Kushanas, were the first to use portraits of rulers. Statement IV is incorrect: many coins were bilingual (e.g., Greek and Pali).

questions.q: Statement I: Early Aryans did not develop a political state structure. Statement II: Rajan was a tribal chief/military leader ruling over people, not a defined area.
o: I is false; II is true
Both are true; II does not explain I
I is true; II is false
Both are true; II explains I
questions.e: Early Aryans were pastoralists; their organization was based on kinship and tribes (Jana), not territorial states. The Rajan was a protector of the tribe, and his power came from military leadership of people rather than land ownership.

questions.q: In context to Buddhism, 'Theris' refers to:
o: Respected women who had attained liberation.
Perfections leading to the Bodhisattva path.
questions.e: 'Theris' refers to respected senior nuns who had attained spiritual liberation (Nirvana). Their experiences are captured in the Therigatha.

questions.q: How many were called gana-sanghas (republican states)? 1️⃣ Vajji 2️⃣ Malla 3️⃣ Anga 4️⃣ Vatsa.
questions.e: Vajji (confederation) and Malla were gana-sanghas where decisions were made by assemblies. Anga and Vatsa were monarchical states with hereditary kings.

questions.q: The terms 'masattuvan' and 'satthavahas' were used for:
o: priestly classes involved in religious activities
learned persons dealing with philosophical matters
officials employed with the royal court
merchants involved in trade of goods
questions.e: These terms referred to successful merchants; 'masattuvan' in Tamil and 'satthavahas' in Prakrit. They traded diverse goods like textiles, salt, and metal.

questions.q: In which region was Dhanyakataka located?
questions.e: Dhanyakataka (modern Dharanikota/Amaravati) was in Andhra Pradesh. It served as the capital of the Satavahana dynasty.

questions.q: Regarding the Neolithic period: 1️⃣ Marked agriculture development and animal domestication 2️⃣ "Ash mounds" are features of the Deccan 3️⃣ Pit houses replaced by burnt brick houses. Which are correct?
questions.e: The Neolithic saw the start of farming and settled life. Ash mounds in South India were pastoral settlements adapting to semi-arid conditions. Statement III is incorrect: Pit houses remained a characteristic feature of sites like Burzahom to escape cold.

questions.q: How many are commonly recognised as Mesolithic sites? 1️⃣ Langhnaj 2️⃣ Sohan valley 3️⃣ Chirand.
questions.e: Langhnaj (Gujarat) is a Mesolithic site. Sohan Valley is a Paleolithic site. Chirand is a prominent Neolithic site.

questions.q: Regarding Rig Vedic society: 1️⃣ Caste basis 2️⃣ Polygamy common among masses 3️⃣ Gotra institution 4️⃣ Women participated in assemblies. Which is correct?
questions.e: Rig Vedic society was based on kinship/clans, not caste. Monogamy was the norm for masses. The institution of Gotra developed later in the Vedic period. Women held an important position and could participate in Sabha and Samiti.

questions.q: How many rows are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Second Council - Pataliputra (Compilation of Pitakas) 2️⃣ Third Council - Rajagriha (Addition of Kathavatthu) 3️⃣ Fourth Council - Kashmir (Division of sects).
questions.e: Row III is correct: Fourth Council (Kashmir, under Kanishka) formalised the Mahayana/Hinayana split. Row I is wrong: First Council was at Rajgriha (Pitakas compiled); Second was at Vaishali. Row II is wrong: Third Council was at Pataliputra.

questions.q: Which statement is correct? 1️⃣ Arhats postpone nirvana to help others 2️⃣ Bodhisattva attains nirvana but doesn't guide others 3️⃣ Sotapanna enters the path and will attain nirvana in few rebirths.
questions.e: Statement III is correct: Sotapanna (Stream-enterer) will attain nirvana within seven rebirths. Statement I is wrong: Bodhisattvas, not Arhats, postpone nirvana for others. Statement II is wrong: Bodhisattvas actively seek to help others.

questions.q: With reference to monoclonal antibodies: 1️⃣ Man-made proteins 2️⃣ Stimulate function by binding to specific antigens 3️⃣ Used in treating viral infections like Nipah. Which are correct?
questions.e: Monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) are lab-created proteins cloned from a single B-cell. They are highly specific, binding to antigens to neutralize pathogens or mark them for destruction. They treat COVID-19 and Ebola; m102.4 has shown potential against Nipah.

questions.q: Regarding germline gene editing: 1️⃣ Modification of reproductive cells/embryos 2️⃣ Passed to future generations 3️⃣ India permitted CRISPR trials for germline. Which are correct?
questions.e: Germline editing targets eggs, sperm, or embryos. These changes are heritable. Statement III is incorrect: India prohibits germline modification for ethical reasons, permitting only non-heritable somatic therapy.

questions.q: BIRSA-101 is:
o: indigenous CRISPR-based gene therapy for sickle cell disease
questions.e: BIRSA-101 is India's first indigenous CRISPR gene therapy for Sickle Cell Disease. It corrects mutations so the body produces normal red blood cells. It was named in honor of Birsa Munda.

questions.q: Which is incorrect regarding missiles?
o: Cruise missiles can only deliver conventional warheads.
Compared to Ballistic missiles, Cruise missiles are harder to detect by radar.
questions.e: Statement I is correct: Cruise missiles fly low, following terrain, making radar detection difficult. Statement II is incorrect: both ballistic and cruise missiles (e.g., BrahMos) can carry both conventional and nuclear warheads.

questions.q: How many pairs are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Dornier-228 - Maritime patrol 2️⃣ IL-76 - Supersonic combat 3️⃣ C-17 - Military transport.
questions.e: Dornier-228 is for maritime patrol/surveillance. C-17 Globemaster III is a strategic cargo/troop lifter. Pair II is incorrect: the IL-76 is a strategic airlifter (heavy transport), not a combat aircraft.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a moderator in a nuclear reactor?
o: To slow down fast-moving neutrons produced during nuclear fission.
To convert nuclear energy directly into electrical energy.
To absorb excess neutrons and stop the chain reaction.
To remove heat from the reactor core to prevent it from excessive heating.
questions.e: Fission produces fast neutrons. A moderator (e.g., heavy water, graphite) slows them down to "thermal" speeds to sustain a controlled chain reaction.

questions.q: Regarding MicroRNA: 1️⃣ Endogenous (encoded within genome) 2️⃣ Short duplex molecules for post-transcriptional gene silencing by targeting mRNA. Which are correct?
questions.e: miRNAs are noncoding RNAs encoded within an organism's own DNA. They regulate gene expression by binding to target mRNAs, leading to their degradation or inhibition of translation.

questions.q: Regarding CAR-T cell therapy: 1️⃣ T-cells engineered with receptors to recognize cancer antigens 2️⃣ Attacks cancer while sparing healthy cells. Which are correct?
questions.e: T-cells are genetically modified to express Chimeric Antigen Receptors (CARs). This allows them to precisely target specific cancer antigens, minimizing damage to normal healthy cells compared to chemotherapy.

questions.q: Regarding Transposons: 1️⃣ "Jumping genes" 2️⃣ Can cause DNA damage/cell death. Which are correct?
questions.e: Transposons are mobile DNA sequences that can insert themselves into different genome regions. They can damage DNA, leading to early cell death, and are considered "tools of evolution" for rearranging the genome.

questions.q: Regarding thorium: Statement I: Thorium can be directly used as fuel. Statement II: Thorium is a 'fertile' material that can be converted into 'fissile' material.
o: I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both true; II does not explain I
questions.e: Statement I is incorrect: Thorium cannot be used directly; it must be converted to Uranium-233 in a reactor. Statement II is correct: Thorium-232 is fertile and transmutes to fissile U-233 after absorbing neutrons.

questions.q: "Membrane Bioreactors" are discussed in the context of:
questions.e: Membrane Bioreactors (MBR) combine biological treatment by microorganisms with membrane filtration. They efficiently remove pollutants, retaining solids and microbes while allowing clean water to pass through.

questions.q: Regarding mRNA vaccines: 1️⃣ Use weakened/killed virus 2️⃣ Do not alter DNA (stay in cytoplasm) 3️⃣ Stored at room temperature long-term. Which is correct?
questions.e: Statement II is correct: mRNA stays in the cytoplasm and never enters the nucleus to interact with DNA. Statement I is incorrect: they use genetic material (mRNA) for a spike protein, not the virus itself. Statement III is incorrect: mRNA is fragile and requires sub-zero storage.

questions.q: Light-microscopy-based Connectomics (LICONN) is associated with:
o: Mapping neural connections in human brain
questions.e: LICONN is a technique to map brain cell connections. It physically expands brain tissue (up to 16x) in a gel so structures can be seen via light microscopy instead of costly electron microscopes.

questions.q: Gene drive technology was recently in news regarding:
questions.e: Gene drive is a process that ensures a specific gene has a near-100% chance of being inherited. Scientists use it to spread infertility or parasite resistance in female Anopheles mosquitoes to collapse populations or stop transmission.

questions.q: Aerial metagenomics refers to:
o: Collecting DNA samples from air in a habitat
Devices to collect blood from moving animals
questions.e: This involves the collection and analysis of genetic material (DNA) from aerosol particles or the air in a specific environment to identify microorganisms present there.

questions.q: INS Arnala, INS Androth and INS Anjadip are:
questions.e: These are indigenously built ASW SWC warships propelled by waterjets. They carry lightweight torpedoes and sonar for detecting and engaging underwater threats.

questions.q: Statement I: SONAR is preferred underwater over RADAR. Statement II: Radio waves are absorbed by seawater; sound waves travel long distances.
o: I is false; II is true
Both true; II does not explain I
I is true; II is false
questions.e: Electromagnetic (radio) waves used in RADAR are strongly attenuated/absorbed by water. Sound waves are mechanical and travel efficiently underwater, making SONAR the primary tool for detecting submerged objects.

questions.q: "Akashteer" is:
o: Indigenous automated air defence control system
questions.e: Akashteer is an automated ADCRS for the Army. It integrates radars and weapons into a single network for real-time tracking and engagement of aerial threats.

questions.q: Statement I: Epigenome editing is safer than CRISPR-Cas9 for some conditions. Statement II: It regulates gene expression without altering the DNA sequence.
o: I is false; II is true
I is true; II is false
Both true; II does not explain I
questions.e: Traditional CRISPR cuts DNA, which is permanent. Epigenome editing uses enzymes to add/remove chemical locks (like methyl groups), making the change reversible and "gentler" as it doesn't break the DNA strands.

questions.q: Regarding Trachoma: 1️⃣ Bacterial infectious disease 2️⃣ Affects respiratory system 3️⃣ India eliminated it as a public health problem. Which are correct?
questions.e: Trachoma is an eye disease caused by Chlamydia trachomatis. It affects the eyelids and cornea, leading to blindness, not the respiratory system. India was validated by WHO in 2024 for eliminating it as a public health problem.

questions.q: "Pumped-storage hydropower" is discussed in context of:
questions.e: This is a hydroelectric energy storage method using two reservoirs at different elevations. Water is discharged to generate power during peak demand and pumped back up when excess energy is available.

questions.q: Regarding Hepatitis D (HDV): 1️⃣ Carcinogenic 2️⃣ Only infects those with Hepatitis B 3️⃣ Mother-to-child transmission possible. Which are correct?
questions.e: HDV is classified as carcinogenic to humans. It is a defective virus requiring HBsAg from Hepatitis B to replicate. It spreads via infected blood, sexual contact, or vertical transmission.

questions.q: Primary function of Regulatory T cells (Tregs) is:
o: To prevent immune system responses against the body's own tissues.
questions.e: Tregs maintain self-tolerance and immune balance by preventing other T-cells from attacking the body’s own proteins (preventing autoimmunity). They also down-regulate the immune response after a threat is cleared.

questions.q: Regarding Fast Breeder Reactors (FBRs): 1️⃣ Use MOX fuel (U-238 and Pu-239) 2️⃣ Heavy water as coolant/moderator. Which is correct?
questions.e: Statement I is correct: FBRs use Uranium-Plutonium MOX fuel and produce more fissile material than they consume. Statement II is incorrect: FBRs use liquid sodium as a coolant and require no moderator.

questions.q: Regarding Nanoparticles: 1️⃣ Only man-made 2️⃣ Metallic oxides used in cosmetics 3️⃣ Environmental entry can be unsafe. Which are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: they exist naturally in volcanic ash and sea spray. Statement 2 is correct: TiO2 and ZnO are used in sunscreens. Statement 3 is correct: diesel exhaust nanoparticles are linked to respiratory issues.

questions.q: Primary objective of 'terminator technology' is to:
o: produce sterile plants with infertile seeds
questions.e: Also known as GURT, this creates sterile plants with seeds that cannot be replanted. This ensures farmers must purchase new seeds for every growing season.

questions.q: Regarding GLP-1 receptor agonists: Statement I: Effective for obesity. Statement II: Slow gastric emptying and increase fullness.
o: Both true; II does not explain I
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
questions.e: Drugs like Semaglutide mimic the GLP-1 hormone. They stimulate insulin but also act on the brain/stomach to delay emptying and suppress appetite, leading directly to weight loss.

questions.q: Regarding Directed Energy Weapons (DEWs): 1️⃣ High-powered lasers 2️⃣ Unaffected by fog/rain 3️⃣ Longer kill range than conventional weapons. Which is correct?
questions.e: Statement I is correct: DEWs use directed energy (lasers) to heat and destroy targets. Statements II and III are incorrect: fog/rain scatter the beams , and their effective range is currently limited to 1-2 km, much shorter than missiles.

questions.q: Passage describes a counter-drone system detecting targets at 6 km using micro munitions:
questions.e: Bhargavastra is an indigenous counter-drone system using a two-layer hard-kill approach: unguided micro-rockets for swarms and guided micro-missiles for precision.

questions.q: Regarding Nuclear Fission vs Fusion: 1️⃣ Fission splits heavy nuclei; Fusion combines light nuclei 2️⃣ Fusion releases more energy per unit mass 3️⃣ Fusion waste is greater/longer-lived. Which are correct?
questions.e: Fusion (e.g., in stars) combines isotopes like Deuterium/Tritium and releases nearly 4x more energy than fission. Statement III is incorrect: fission produces long-lived radioactive waste, while fusion produces inert helium.

questions.q: Regarding Carbon fibres: 1️⃣ Used in automobiles/aircraft 2️⃣ Cannot be recycled. Which is correct?
questions.e: Carbon fibers are used for high strength and low weight in planes and efficient vehicles. Statement 2 is incorrect: they can be recycled (often used in tennis rackets), though the process is difficult.

questions.q: How many stages of India’s nuclear programme are correctly matched? 1️⃣ First - PHWR (produce plutonium) 2️⃣ Second - FBR (breed more fuel) 3️⃣ Third - Thorium utilization.
questions.e: First stage uses natural uranium in PHWRs to produce plutonium. Second stage uses Pu in FBRs to breed more fissile material. Third stage uses abundant thorium to transmute into U-233.

questions.q: How many contribute significantly to Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR)? 1️⃣ Indiscriminate antibiotics use 2️⃣ Premature discontinuation 3️⃣ Excessive vitamin supplements 4️⃣ GM crop consumption 5️⃣ Antimicrobial drugs in livestock.
questions.e: Options I, II, and V are major drivers. Misuse in humans and use for growth in livestock creates resistant bacteria. Vitamins (III) and GM crops (IV) have no known scientific link to AMR.

questions.q: The term 'Twigstats' refers to:
o: tool to study individual-level genetic ancestry
questions.e: Twigstats analyzes ancient DNA samples with high precision to trace migration patterns and ancestry, such as the genetic legacy of Vikings in Europe.

questions.q: How many are "Distributed Energy Resources"? 1️⃣ Battery storage 2️⃣ Biomass generators 3️⃣ Fuel cells 4️⃣ Rooftop solar.
questions.e: DERs are small (typically <10 MW) modular generation/storage technologies installed on-site. All listed items, including EV batteries exporting to the grid, are examples.

questions.q: 'Black Mass Recovery Technology' is used for:
o: extraction of metals from lithium-ion batteries
questions.e: "Black mass" is a powder from recycled Li-ion batteries rich in lithium, cobalt, and nickel. This technology extracts these valuable materials to reduce import reliance.

questions.q: Regarding Stem Cells: 1️⃣ Unspecialised; one daughter remains a stem cell, other differentiates 2️⃣ Only in embryos 3️⃣ HSCs are totipotent. Which is correct?
questions.e: Stem cells are undifferentiated and can divide asymmetrically. Statement II is wrong: they are also in adult tissues (bone marrow, liver). Statement III is wrong: HSCs are multipotent (making blood cells), whereas totipotent cells (like zygotes) can make any cell type.

questions.q: Which vaccine contains weakened pathogens that cannot cause disease?
questions.e: Live attenuated vaccines (e.g., oral polio) use genetically weakened pathogens that replicate enough to trigger a broad immune response without causing illness. Inactivated vaccines use "killed" pathogens.

questions.q: Regarding GM mustard DMH-11: 1️⃣ Hybrid of 'Varuna' and 'Early Heera-2' 2️⃣ Second GM crop allowed for commercial cultivation in India. Which is correct?
questions.e: DMH-11 was created using barnase-barstar technology by crossing 'Varuna' and 'Early Heera-2'. Statement II is incorrect: Bt cotton remains the only GM crop commercially cultivated in India; GM mustard faced legal challenges.

questions.q: Regarding National Biofoundry Network: 1️⃣ Launched under BioE3 Policy 2️⃣ Objective to strengthen indigenous biomanufacturing. Which are correct?
questions.e: Launched under the BioE3 Policy, this network of six institutions aims to boost India's bioeconomy and foster sustainable biotechnology innovations.

questions.q: How many of the following are fifth generation fighter aircraft? 1️⃣ Rafael 2️⃣ MiG-29 3️⃣ Tejas MK-1.
questions.e: Fifth-gen fighters (e.g., F-22, F-35, J-20) feature stealth, supercruise, and advanced data fusion. Rafael, MiG-29, and Tejas MK-1 are all fourth-generation (4.5th) jets.

questions.q: In Biotechnology, what is the primary function of restriction enzymes?
o: Translation of genetic information into proteins.
Separation of DNA fragments based on their size.
Making cuts at specific positions within the DNA.
questions.e: Known as "molecular scissors," these enzymes (endonucleases) inspect DNA sequences and cut the double helix at specific recognition points (palindromes).

questions.q: Regarding Organ-on-Chip technology: 1️⃣ Small device recreating organ functions in microenvironment 2️⃣ Reduces animal testing 3️⃣ Helps in precision therapeutics. Which are correct?
questions.e: These devices use human cells to mimic organ environments. They provide more accurate drug testing results than animal models and allow for drugs tailored to individual patient needs.

questions.q: Which is an example of 'Xenotransplantation'?
o: Infusion of non-human animal cells or organs into human recipients.
Inactivation of genes in human body.
questions.e: Xenotransplantation involves using live non-human animal cells, tissues, or organs (e.g., pig heart valves or kidneys) to heal human recipients.

questions.q: Regarding bio-toilets in Indian Railways: 1️⃣ Decomposition by fungal inoculum 2️⃣ Ammonia and water vapour are the only end products. Which are correct?
questions.e: Both are incorrect. Degradation is performed by Anaerobic Bacteria. The end products are water and inflammable Methane gas.

questions.q: Regarding Carbon Nanotubes (CNTs): 1️⃣ 3D tubular structures with pentagonal arrangement 2️⃣ High electrical/thermal conductivity 3️⃣ Targeted drug delivery. Which are correct?
questions.e: Statement I is incorrect: CNTs are 1D tubular structures with a hexagonal carbon arrangement. They are characterized by extreme tensile strength and high conductivities. They are used in targeted drug delivery and biosensors.

questions.q: How many are applications of nuclear technology? 1️⃣ Developing disease-resistant crops 2️⃣ Pest management 3️⃣ Diagnosis/therapy of thyroid cancer.
questions.e: Crops are irradiated to initiate genetic diversity. The Sterile Insect Technique (SIT) manages pests. Radioisotopes like Iodine-131 are used in cancer diagnosis and therapy.

questions.q: Regarding Trans Fats: 1️⃣ Type of unsaturated fatty acids 2️⃣ Only produced artificially 3️⃣ Permissible limit in India is 5% 4️⃣ Increase cardiovascular risk. Which are correct?
questions.e: Trans fats are unsaturated fatty acids. Statement II is incorrect: they occur naturally in ruminant meat/dairy. Statement III is incorrect: FSSAI reduced the limit to 2% from 2022 onwards. Statement IV is correct: high intake significantly raises heart disease risk.

questions.q: How many are classified as Ballistic missiles? 1️⃣ Brahmos 2️⃣ Akash Prime 3️⃣ Prithvi 4️⃣ Agni-V.
questions.e: Prithvi (short-range) and Agni-V (intercontinental) are ballistic missiles following an arched trajectory. Brahmos is a cruise missile and Akash Prime is a surface-to-air missile.

questions.q: The primary concern about glycans in viral infections like HIV is that they:
o: are sugar shields masking viral proteins from immune system
questions.e: HIV surface proteins are covered by host-derived complex sugars called a "glycan shield". This hides the virus from the immune system, blocks antibody binding, and makes vaccine development difficult.
